issue_context.title: Difficulty to explore the resource page @ https://angular.io/resources
issue_context.body:
# 📚 Docs or angular.io bug report ### Description **EXPLORE ANGULAR RESOURCES** @ https://angular.io/resources needs to be sturctured to be able to navigate to all resources with improved user experience. A lone scroll bar in this page will not help the reader a great deal in exploring the resources. ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction Go to https://angular.io/resources ### What's the affected URL?** https://angular.io/... ### Reproduction Steps** ### Expected vs Actual Behavior** User should be able to nagivate the various aspects of the angular resources with ease. The current page is unable to provide a glimpse of all the resources at one place as well. ## 📷Screenshot ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46414819/68012666-aee1fb80-fcb0-11e9-8c9f-10977841894e.png) ## 🔥 Exception or Error
## 🌍 Your Environment ### Browser info ### Anything else relevant?
comments:
Quite true. The resources page is getting unwieldy.
We should at least have a Table of Contents in there. Possibly also break the page up into multiple tabs (e.g. `Development`, `Education`, `Community`), similar to the [contributors page][1].

[1]: https://angular.io/about
@bhargava-raju can I help you on this
@bhargava-raju @gkalpak I think for the first change we can just convert the headings into expansion panels.
Not sure what you mean, @ajitsinghkaler? Can you elaborate?

![Expansion Panel   Angular Material](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/39260684/68781063-363e5000-065d-11ea-85b3-c0bf16783613.png)

Something like this I wanted to suggest an expansion panel for all the headings in the angular resources page.

@gkalpak Yeah we can add tabs but we have two levels of headings even then we may have to use something like this. 

Like for development, the education, the community we may use tabs but for the rest, we can use expansion panels.  What are your thoughts on this.

Let's take is one step at a time :smiley: 
I would say let's split them up by the first level and then we can decide what to do on the second level if/when needed.

I agree with @gkalpak - tabs would be great as we have on the https://angular.io/about page. 

I also suggest adding an "ALL" tab so that someone can easily search through something they are looking for in particular.

This would be a great next step and improvement from what we have.
